summary: Independent live-UI verification of the RETRY-BUTTON F12-hijack path on https://bin-context-pat.preview.emergentagent.com. Logged in as test@aurem.dev via real /login form; on /dashboard, injected a genuine console.error (Uncaught TypeError ... at js:317) that F12ErrorCapture.js captured (window.__auremF12.hasErrors() === true). Intercepted the FIRST /chat/stream POST and fulfilled it with a fake SSE done frame carrying turn_state=error + failure_mode=provider_rate_or_5xx, which correctly caused MessageBubble to render the data-testid='turn-retry-btn'. Confirmed the FIRST (fresh-compose) request DID carry a populated f12_payload with the js:317 console_error (baseline correct — the fresh-compose path still forwards F12). Clicked the retry button; the SECOND /chat/stream POST was NOT intercepted (route.continue_) and hit the real backend. Captured the retry request body byte-for-byte and the real backend response body.
seed_data_creation: None — used the pre-seeded TEST_bug2_ui session and p_demo_a project already on the account.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The chat surface is at /dashboard (not /ora). The chat send endpoint is POST /api/aurem-dev/chat/stream (SSE), NOT /chat/send as the review request mentioned. To force the failed-turn UI state deterministically, intercept /chat/stream and fulfill with an SSE body containing a done frame with turn_state='error' and failure_mode='provider_rate_or_5xx' (do NOT use provider_filtered — that path suppresses the retry button, see MessageBubble.jsx line 1100). The retry button only renders when m.turnState==='error' AND m.failureMode!=='provider_filtered'.

test_a_retry_request_f12_payload.captured_retry_request_body_verbatim: {"prompt":"update the footer text to say contact us today","session_id":"TEST_bug2_ui_0d3851b9","max_tool_iters":2,"maxx_mode":false,"agent":"auto","mode":"swift","execution_mode":"prompt","project_id":"p_demo_a","f12_payload":null,"ora_panel":false,"screenshot_b64":null}
test_a_retry_request_f12_payload.conclusion: The Retry button's request explicitly sets f12_payload=null. Frontend-side gate (ChatPanel.jsx L2464-2470, promptOverride!=null → f12Payload=null) works correctly in the live UI.

test_b_real_backend_retry_reply.captured_retry_response_body_verbatim: {"detail":"The connection to your website's code isn't available right now — it may have been disconnected or doesn't cover this project. Open Projects → APP to reconnect."}
test_b_real_backend_retry_reply.conclusion: The real backend's response to the retry contains ZERO reference to js:317, the injected TypeError, 'debugging', or any console-error content. It is a GitHub-App scope pre-check 403 (unrelated to F12) — proof that the F12 payload never reached backend classify_intent(); if the pre-fix Mode-D hijack were still live, the backend would have needed a non-null f12_payload to hit that path, which is impossible now given (a).

baseline_first_request_had_f12_populated.note: The intercepted (mocked-fulfill) FIRST /chat/stream request DID carry a populated f12_payload.console_errors array with the injected js:317 message, confirming the fresh-compose path still forwards F12 (baseline correct — retry vs fresh-compose divergence is intentional).

verification_evidence.retry_button_visibility: PASS — data-testid='turn-retry-btn' rendered on the assistant bubble after the mocked failed turn; screenshot at /app/test_reports/screenshots/retry_btn_ok.png shows 'This failed — provider_5xx. The provider was busy — safe to retry now. [Retry]' bubble.

rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no bug found in this round. The retry-button F12-hijack fix is verified live via UI: retry-button click sends f12_payload:null, and the real backend response contains no reference to the injected browser error, confirming the frontend-side gate at ChatPanel.jsx L2464-2470 (promptOverride!=null → f12Payload=null) and the backend-side gate at chat_helpers.classify_intent (references_environment_signal() gate) are both intact end-to-end in production preview.
